cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight the expansive open-world setting and car selection, alongside mandatory account logins and purchase issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a massive open-world map set in Japan with a large selection of cars.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Forza Horizon 6 – Japan Was Worth the Wait[/h1]

Forza Horizon finally went to Japan.

That’s it. We can all go home now.

[b]Forza Horizon 6[/b] is basically Playground Games taking the same dangerously addictive formula, putting it in Japan, adding 550+ cars, and somehow convincing me that driving aimlessly for two hours counts as productivity.

And you know what?
It works.

[b]The Good:[/b]
- Japan is easily one of the best Horizon maps ever made. Tokyo, mountains, touge roads, countryside — finally my Initial D delusions have somewhere to live.
- Driving still feels fantastic: arcade enough to relax, realistic enough to blame yourself when you enter a corner at 240 km/h.
- Tokyo is HUGE and actually feels like a city instead of six buildings pretending to be one.
- 550+ cars means I will still drive the same 12 cars for 90% of my playtime.
- Runs surprisingly well and looks absolutely gorgeous.
- Touge battles. Enough said.

[b]The Not-So-Good:[/b]
- Customization still feels weirdly behind other racing games.
- Forza Aero continues its lifelong mission to make beautiful cars uglier.
- Festival Playlist FOMO is still here because apparently having a job is considered a skill issue.
- At its core, this is still [i]Forza Horizon[/i]. Bigger, prettier, better — but not revolutionary.

[b]Final Verdict:[/b]
Forza Horizon 6 doesn't reinvent the wheel.

It just puts TE37s on it, sends it down a Japanese mountain at 180 km/h, and plays Eurobeat in my head.

And frankly, that's all I wanted.

[b]9/10[/b] – Man chooses vroom vroom. Man drives through Japan. Man happy.

One of the best games in the series. The physics are refined compared to prior FH games, the map is huge and simultaneously dense, the car list is full of fun and interesting cars, and the writing and progression is more down to earth compared to the lunacy of FH4 and FH5. My only issues come down to performance on my system and sacrificing a more realistic sense of population density in Japan for gameplay (Tokyo should not feel like Coeur d'Alene Idaho).
Best Forza Horizon game I have played the graphics are amazing and the map is massive

cohorts.label: 20-100h

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the map and scenery of Japan are visually stunning and the highlight of the game.

citations.review_text:
The first thing that caught me was the visuals. Japan looks absolutely beautiful. The scenery, roads, cities, mountains, and overall atmosphere make simply driving around feel like an experience on its own. Sometimes I find myself slowing down just to enjoy the view.

Then there are the cars. The selection is great, and seeing them in such a beautiful environment makes every car feel special. Whether you're cruising around or pushing a car to its limits, there's always something satisfying about being behind the wheel.

But what I enjoy the most is the feeling of driving*

There's something incredibly satisfying about accelerating through a corner, feeling the car respond to your inputs, and hearing the engine scream as you push it harder. The car sounds are especially good. Different cars actually feel different, and hearing the engine, exhaust, and gear shifts while driving makes the experience much more immersive.

For me, Forza Horizon 6 isn't just about racing.

It's about driving a car you like, finding a beautiful road, and simply enjoying the moment.

The visuals, cars, driving feel, and sound all come together really well.

Sometimes, I don't even want to race. I just want to drive.

9/10 — Beautiful, satisfying, and incredibly fun to drive.

I'll be quite honest here. The map is very beautiful and the best in the Horizon series so far. That's the only plus of the game, it gets boring fast as it's really just a reskin of FH4 and FH5 with a few new features. There is no progression, you get showered with money and cars and once you get your gold wristband? It's back to the fomo festival playlist we've had since FH4. If you are new to Horizon then I'd say go for it, the game is visually stunning, If you are a long time fan then I'd just avoid it since gameplay wise it adds nothing new unless you really want to drive in Japan.

citations.review_text:
- Another Horizon game, where they simply changed the festival location to Japan.
And what do you think? Will you see any JDM here? Of course not.
- Tokyo may be good, but of the 25 road races in the game, only 4 are inside the city itself.
- What comes to mind when it comes to Japan and cars is, of course, drifting. So, of the 20 drift zones, 10 of them take place on dirt roads. Very cool.
- The advertising campaign mentioned car encounters, but at the game's release, they're completely empty and dead.
- The car physics, which many call "Simcade", are absolutely ridiculous. Just look at how the car bounces up and down hills like a piece of rock – it's absolutely ridiculous – no suspension softness whatsoever.
- Now let's remember, at the end of FH5's life cycle, we had 900 cars in the fleet, but here we have just over 600 cars again, and then the developers will add more old car models from the Motorsport and Horizon series, labeled "NEW car," which haven't even been redesigned for the new game.
Not really feeling this one compared to FH5. I'm not the biggest fan of off-road racing and it seems like thats what 95% of the races are in this game.

citations.review_text:
before going with the review i want to clarify that i love forza horizon series, i've been playing the game since the 3rd game and loving it.. i didn't play the previous 2 games because i do not own an xbox. 

6 is probably FH fans wet dream comes true, since 4 we always speculate that the next festival venue is japan but instead we got UK/Ireland and Mexico, both are good map. map itself is beautiful, its a miniature version of Tokyo and its surrounding, and its finely crafted by the team at PG. but alas if you play the game since the 3rd game a lot of feature have been removed.

they removed ranked mode on the 4th game. my issue was why removed? why not make it optional? so people who are casual players dont need to participate if they dont want to. but the ones that are enjoying the mode can always go at it.

then they remove clubs, which i think it ties to a microsoft api called x ox for windows live if im not mistaken. it was removed late on the 5th game lifespan, making player confused why we cannot add more players to our clubs. it requires us to download an app to manage club which that app are now removed. and also the features itself.. i was thinking they might fix this in 6... which i was wrong,... 

they gave us a pretty map but felt lifeless, they gave us car meets but we can only park and talk using premade texts. imagine if we can chat on car meets, meet new car guys, arranging races, from randos became friends, create car clubs, recruit members... nope they just simply remove it and gave us a lifeless maps.

game itself are great but with no social features some if the feature the provide felt useless... somehow i felt its just a nice map but features are even less than previous games. i still plat it though, i still do my weekly runs with my friends, since this game is the only social bridge for me and my friends since i live abroad.

hope you guys can improve the game even better than the previous games and worthy of the title forza horizon... 



…

Good but not great as it could have been. 3 months into the game's life and there's still some pretty embarrassing bugs. Several visual glitches on cars, along with car engine audio problems where the race exhaust sounds are heavily muted. Additionally the sport and race transmission sound is needlessly loud. Another glaring issue is the save corruption issue, which has affected many players both on PC and console and is entirely luck of the draw if it happens to you or not. That issue has been acknowledged by the devs and patches have been done to correct the problem, but it still remains an ongoing issue. On a personal note, I don't care for how heavily nerfed CR rewards for races and wheelspin rewards are, I find it makes the game very grindy and makes doing actual races feel like a waste of time. Another issue I have is the NPC traffic is unnecessarily dense outside of the city area, even on dirt trails, and finally it rains waaaay too much regardless of what season it is. Get ready to just sit and wait for 10 plus minutes for a rain squall to pass so you can do a dry drag race or time attack run!

On a positive note the map is gorgeous and expansive and I'm quite impressed with Tokyo city and the intricate highway interchanges. The new cars added have been pretty good and I'm sure even more interesting choices will be added over the game's lifespan. Handling has also been improved over FH5. The game is honestly good and I do recommend it if you like the other Forza Horizon games, and while there are some issues, there's a good possibility that those issues will be fixed in a later patch or update.

claims.claim: Reviewers report a lack of exclusive road or street racing modes, with many events dominated by cross-country or dirt races.

citations.review_text:
[b][u]Apparently JDM Stands For Japanese Dirt Motorsport[/u][/b] 
(needs an exclusive road/street race option to online racing)

I am a massive fan of Japanese car culture, so already you know my opinion is more valid and important than not only recent or seasonal fans of Forza Horizon, but also long-term fans who think the year they first played Forza gives their opinion more weight on the latest release we can all play.

It doesn't.

So what is my experience with Japanese car culture? I've seen some of it. Perhaps I have seen all of it, but perhaps not. I have watched YouTube Shorts of Japanese cars going sideways, for example, which is basically the same as having lived in Japan.

I've also played some racing games before, including several of the previous Forza Horizon games, so I feel I have a reasonably comprehensive understanding of what a Japanese-themed racing game should probably contain.

And what it should contain is road racing.

Unfortunately, Forza Horizon 6 has decided that what Japan really needs is supercars doing Cross Country.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Road & Street Racing[/h2]

My main gripe with Forza Horizon 6 is that, despite being a Japanese-themed racing game, there’s no exclusive road or street racing mode.

Before anyone says "just play custom races": I know they exist. The custom race lobbies are mostly dead, which isn't really a solution when nobody joins your Alien Race Mode setup.

This is apparently difficult to understand, so I'll explain it using advanced engineering terminology:

[b]I want to race on roads.[/b]

That's it.

It feels like around 70% of the races and games I get matchmade into are Cross Country and Rally events, often in S1 and above. So you end up racing top-of-the-range supercars across mountain fields and dirt roads.

Very Japanese.

I see them doing this all the time in YouTube Shorts.

The other gripe is Touge events, where again you're mostly being put into S1 and above.

Very Japanese to be racing Ferraris, Lamborghini…

The customization is too limited (most of them are forza front bumper and forza spoiler), everyone car looks the same. I think that's why the car meet is dead. Chance to get rare car from wheelspin is lower than pull a ssr from a gacha game. We r in Japan but most event is offroad.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that multiplayer sessions suffer from heavy ramming and griefing by other players.

citations.review_text:
At it's core this could be a brilliant game that you'd play for years.

Unfortunately, it suffers from a number of issues, and an insulting lack of content, that become more and more frustrating the longer you play.

[b]Very poor rewards, and recycling of rewards, even by Season 2[/b]
Reward cars are being recycled already. We're in Season 3 or 4 now, I forget, and all rewards are cars I already have.  For the ridiculous amount I paid for this game with all the extras, I am pretty peed off by the fact I've run out of content, and all rewards are cars I already have 2 times over.

...and the [i]Wheelspins[/i]. Crikey. I've got 30m+ in the bank and all I get from Wheelspins is pocket change - 5k, 10k, maybe 100k if I'm really lucky.  Rare car? Unlikely. Legendary car? Well, 400hours on this and I haven't had [i]a single Legendary car in a Wheelspin[/i].

[b]Ramming and griefers[/b]
The Ramming is [i]out of control[/i] in Multiplayer. 9 out of 10 lobbies will have at least one ramming moron who is only there to ruin your race. And they do, constantly.

Yet PG won't do anything to stop people doing it, additionally making Reporting such a drag that you can't face it.  So what is it PG? Ramming okay? or illegal? You ban people for doing it but only after being sent a damn montage of the perpetrator in action, which takes an age to pick through a clip to trim it down to mere nanoseconds of footage so you can upload it to the highly restrictive Reporting Form, which never tells you the Upload limit OR the accepted filetypes, you have to guess it.

And no proactive actions on PG's part to prevent it or make sure players are aware of this 'rule'.

[b]Bugs are constant and infuriating. [/b]
SO many times I've lost a race due to stupid bugs. The main source of fury is how often you can *just clip* a barrier with a wing mirror or bumper, and come to an immediate, absolute stop.  250mph to zero, instantly, after the mildest touch of a wall or barrier. I've also had a full-stop c…

Unenjoyable multiplayer experience. Everyone rams you, cheats, or does both, and they're never banned. If you thought the game would be different, do not fall for it. It's got the same issues FH5 had, and it carried over to this game. Auctions are swarmed with bots, you can't customize nearly as much as you want. If you're playing with friends like me it's unenjoyable.

-The AI drivers are super inconsistent. Gong a single difficulty higher or lower can be the difference between being curb stomped or racing past all drivers in the first corner. The open world AI is also very jittery and broken.

Now past those 100 hours came the end-game content. And, oh boy...

The economy in this game was alright at acceptable at launch. I got a quite a few cars from the story and by playing the first festival playlist. I "used to" get a nice amount of wheelspins. "Used to". Once you finish the main story, you barely get anything. And as for the credits you get for playing the game. It is also almost non-existent in comparison with the more high end cars Playground games expects you to grind for. And every way of obtaining money or wheelspins. A glitch, exploit or just an in-game feature as been nerfed to oblivion. The auction house is also broken and some cars are locked behind wheelspins. You are not meant to get all the cars in the game. At least not without months or years of grinding a gameplay loop that is JUST NOT FUN. PGG just want's you to buy their car passes.

As for the wheelspins and why they are no longer fun.
-First, you barely get any.
-Second, the quality of the wheelspins has been diluted even further with more clothes, horns and a ♥♥♥♥ ton of common 5K credit rewards.
-and Third, Is that seemingly common cars like the Nissan 240SX and many super and hyper cars can only be obtained through wheelspins. So you are kind of forced to somehow go throu…

Good but not great as it could have been. 3 months into the game's life and there's still some pretty embarrassing bugs. Several visual glitches on cars, along with car engine audio problems where the race exhaust sounds are heavily muted. Additionally the sport and race transmission sound is needlessly loud. Another glaring issue is the save corruption issue, which has affected many players both on PC and console and is entirely luck of the draw if it happens to you or not. That issue has been acknowledged by the devs and patches have been done to correct the problem, but it still remains an ongoing issue. On a personal note, I don't care for how heavily nerfed CR rewards for races and wheelspin rewards are, I find it makes the game very grindy and makes doing actual races feel like a waste of time. Another issue I have is the NPC traffic is unnecessarily dense outside of the city area, even on dirt trails, and finally it rains waaaay too much regardless of what season it is. Get ready to just sit and wait for 10 plus minutes for a rain squall to pass so you can do a dry drag race or time attack run!

On a positive note the map is gorgeous and expansive and I'm quite impressed with Tokyo city and the intricate highway interchanges. The new cars added have been pretty good and I'm sure even more interesting choices will be added over the game's lifespan. Handling has also been improved over FH5. The game is honestly good and I do recommend it if you like the other Forza Horizon games, and while there are some issues, there's a good possibility that those issues will be fixed in a later patch or update.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the multiplayer experience is plagued by rampant cheating and unpunished ramming.

citations.review_text:
At it's core this could be a brilliant game that you'd play for years.

Unfortunately, it suffers from a number of issues, and an insulting lack of content, that become more and more frustrating the longer you play.

[b]Very poor rewards, and recycling of rewards, even by Season 2[/b]
Reward cars are being recycled already. We're in Season 3 or 4 now, I forget, and all rewards are cars I already have.  For the ridiculous amount I paid for this game with all the extras, I am pretty peed off by the fact I've run out of content, and all rewards are cars I already have 2 times over.

...and the [i]Wheelspins[/i]. Crikey. I've got 30m+ in the bank and all I get from Wheelspins is pocket change - 5k, 10k, maybe 100k if I'm really lucky.  Rare car? Unlikely. Legendary car? Well, 400hours on this and I haven't had [i]a single Legendary car in a Wheelspin[/i].

[b]Ramming and griefers[/b]
The Ramming is [i]out of control[/i] in Multiplayer. 9 out of 10 lobbies will have at least one ramming moron who is only there to ruin your race. And they do, constantly.

Yet PG won't do anything to stop people doing it, additionally making Reporting such a drag that you can't face it.  So what is it PG? Ramming okay? or illegal? You ban people for doing it but only after being sent a damn montage of the perpetrator in action, which takes an age to pick through a clip to trim it down to mere nanoseconds of footage so you can upload it to the highly restrictive Reporting Form, which never tells you the Upload limit OR the accepted filetypes, you have to guess it.

And no proactive actions on PG's part to prevent it or make sure players are aware of this 'rule'.

[b]Bugs are constant and infuriating. [/b]
SO many times I've lost a race due to stupid bugs. The main source of fury is how often you can *just clip* a barrier with a wing mirror or bumper, and come to an immediate, absolute stop.  250mph to zero, instantly, after the mildest touch of a wall or barrier. I've also had a full-stop c…

Unenjoyable multiplayer experience. Everyone rams you, cheats, or does both, and they're never banned. If you thought the game would be different, do not fall for it. It's got the same issues FH5 had, and it carried over to this game. Auctions are swarmed with bots, you can't customize nearly as much as you want. If you're playing with friends like me it's unenjoyable.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that launching and playing the game is hindered by Xbox app and Microsoft authentication service errors.

citations.review_text:
Game was OK till one day the Xbox app broke.

Forza uses "gaming services" to authenticate, and if there's ever any issue with that, no Microslop game will launch regardless of where you purchased it.

All their customer service is AI now, and if a few common sense things dont work, the AI just starts saying there's nothing that can be done to fix it by you or the AI, and that it cant contact a human.  It then gets stuck in a loop where it tells you the problem is unfixable, then denies the problem is unfixable before immediately declaring the issue unfixable.

Microslop is just fine with a percentage of their customers arbitrarily losing the ability to play any Microslop game for undetermined amounts of time.  If you see Microsoft attached to any game, dont purchase it.  Your ability to play depends on how well Microsoft knows how to program computers, and that's not very well.

Edit:

What worked was:

1. Go to Task Manager, and "end task" for Gaming Services and Xbox App.

2. In Settings/Apps try to "repair" Gaming Services.

3. It wont go thru, but it makes the Xbox App realize there is an issue.

4. Open Xbox App.

5. Install the update Xbox App prompts.

6. It will then open and actually sign in, it will also eventually sign out, but it gets you far enough to play Steam games.

It's worked a few days, but I wont be surprised if/when it starts messing up again.

It's not worth the hassle of dealing with this, and since it can happen to any Microsoft game that goes for every Microsoft game.  Maybe if no one buys their games, they'll stop adding all this nonsense.

Keep crashing range from 2 hours to 5 minutes after launch the game. I use the latest driver, update windows 10 to latest patch, never install Afterburner or any kind of that program. It always crash with FHC03, and always disable GPU until I restart my laptop. I'm not sure if I will complete trial since it keep crashing during 2nd or 3rd races. It's borderline unplayable.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that cloud saves can become corrupted, resulting in lost progression that support cannot restore.

citations.review_text:
I genuinely enjoyed Forza Horizon 6 and had a great time with it for the first few weeks. Unfortunately, after 159 hours of playtime, my cloud save became corrupted and I lost all of my progress.

I contacted Forza Support and spent quite a while troubleshooting the problem on both my Windows PC and Steam Deck. Eventually, I was told that my original save could not be recovered and that I would have to delete it and start over. Support can restore my inventory, but not my actual game progress.

To make matters worse, initially I couldn't even start over because the game kept trying to synchronize the broken cloud save. After trying numerous fixes, clearing the Steam download cache finally allowed me to select my new local save, so I can at least play the game again.

However, that doesn't change the fact that I've lost 159 hours of progression through no fault of my own and now have to replay everything from the beginning.

I really enjoyed FH6 before this happened, and the game itself is great when it works. But a cloud-save system capable of permanently losing nearly 160 hours of progress, with no way for support to restore that progression, is a serious enough issue that I cannot recommend the game.

If the save system is improved or my progress can eventually be restored, I would gladly reconsider this review. But right now, losing 159 hours is simply too significant to ignore.
